faqs.q: How much does a Slovensky Cuvac cost to buy?
faqs.a: Reputable breeders typically charge $1,200–$4,000 for a Slovensky Cuvac puppy. Prices vary by breeder reputation, health testing, and lineage. Rescue adoption fees are typically $100–$500 and include vaccinations, neutering, and microchipping.

faqs.q: What is the monthly cost of owning a Slovensky Cuvac?
faqs.a: Budget $200–$400 per month for a Slovensky Cuvac, covering food, preventive vet care, insurance, grooming and supplies. Large breeds cost more across every category — food portions, medication doses and professional services all scale with weight.

faqs.q: What are the biggest ongoing costs for a Slovensky Cuvac?
faqs.a: The three largest annual expenses are food ($800–1,200), veterinary care ($400–$1,200 budgeted annually), and pet insurance ($800–1,800 per year). Grooming adds $400–$1,200 annually for Slovensky Cuvacs due to their coat type.

faqs.q: How much does a Slovensky Cuvac cost in the first year?
faqs.a: Year one costs for a Slovensky Cuvac are significantly higher than subsequent years, typically $2,500–$5,000. This covers the purchase price or adoption fee, initial vet checks, vaccinations, spay/neuter, microchipping, crate, bedding, collar, leads and puppy training classes.

faqs.q: How often should I groom a Slovensky Cuvac?
faqs.a: Slovensky Cuvacs need brushing 3–5 times per week, daily during seasonal coat blows. The dense undercoat requires a dedicated undercoat rake, not just a surface slicker brush. Nails should be trimmed every 3–4 weeks. Ears should be checked and cleaned monthly.

faqs.q: Do Slovensky Cuvacs shed a lot?
faqs.a: Yes — they are considered heavy shedders. Regular brushing is the most effective control tool. A slicker brush and undercoat rake are both essential for Slovensky Cuvacs. Deshedding treatments from professional groomers can reduce seasonal shedding temporarily.

faqs.q: What grooming tools does a Slovensky Cuvac need?
faqs.a: A slicker brush for surface debris and an undercoat rake for the dense undercoat are both essential. A shedding blade or deshedding tool helps during heavy moult periods. A nail grinder is useful if your Slovensky Cuvac is sensitive to clippers.

faqs.q: How often should I bathe a Slovensky Cuvac?
faqs.a: Every 4–6 weeks is appropriate for most Slovensky Cuvacs that live indoors. More frequent bathing is needed if they swim or spend time in mud. Over-bathing strips natural skin oils — use a pH-balanced dog shampoo rather than human products.

faqs.q: Are Slovensky Cuvacs easy to train?
faqs.a: Slovensky Cuvacs are considered easier to train than average — they respond quickly to reward-based methods and generalise cues well. Short 10–15 minute sessions outperform long correction-heavy drills.

faqs.q: What training method works best for a Slovensky Cuvac?
faqs.a: Reward-based training using treats, praise and toy rewards is the most effective and well-researched approach for Slovensky Cuvacs. Keep sessions short and positive, end on a success, and vary your rewards to maintain engagement.

faqs.q: At what age should I start training my Slovensky Cuvac?
faqs.a: Start training from the day your puppy arrives home, typically at 8 weeks. The 8–16 week window is the most sensitive socialisation period. Enrol in a puppy class within the first two weeks for structured socialisation alongside basic obedience foundations.

faqs.q: How long does it take to train a Slovensky Cuvac?
faqs.a: Most Slovensky Cuvacs learn basic obedience cues (sit, stay, come, down) within 2–4 weeks of daily practice. Reliable recall in distracting environments typically takes 2–3 months of consistent reinforcement.

faqs.q: What health problems do Slovensky Cuvacs commonly have?
faqs.a: Slovensky Cuvacs are most commonly associated with routine age-related conditions. Regular vet checks, appropriate weight management, and breed-specific screening tests help detect issues early. Ask any breeder for health test results before purchasing.

faqs.q: How long do Slovensky Cuvacs live?
faqs.a: Slovensky Cuvacs have an average lifespan of 11–13 years. Larger breeds typically have shorter lifespans than smaller breeds. Maintaining a healthy weight and regular vet care are the most impactful factors for longevity.

faqs.q: Are Slovensky Cuvacs prone to hip dysplasia?
faqs.a: Slovensky Cuvacs have a moderate-to-elevated risk of hip dysplasia, particularly for large or active breeds. Ask for OFA or PennHIP hip evaluation certificates when buying from a breeder. Weight control and avoiding high-impact exercise during bone growth (under 18 months) reduces risk.

faqs.q: What health tests should a Slovensky Cuvac puppy have?
faqs.a: At minimum, your Slovensky Cuvac puppy should have a vet health check, first vaccinations, deworming, and microchipping before coming home. Ask the breeder for parent health certificates relevant to Slovensky Cuvac-specific conditions. A vet check within 72 hours of bringing your puppy home is recommended to establish a baseline.

faqs.q: Are Slovensky Cuvacs good with kids?
faqs.a: Slovensky Cuvacs can be protective and may be cautious around unfamiliar children. Early socialisation with children from puppyhood significantly improves tolerance. Always supervise interactions between dogs and young children.

faqs.q: Do Slovensky Cuvacs get along with other dogs?
faqs.a: Slovensky Cuvacs can be selective with other dogs due to their protective nature. Early socialisation in puppy classes and controlled on-lead introductions with other dogs help build positive associations.

faqs.q: Do Slovensky Cuvacs bark a lot?
faqs.a: Slovensky Cuvacs tend to be vocal — they may bark at strangers, sounds, or when under-stimulated. Adequate daily exercise and mental enrichment (training sessions, puzzle feeders) significantly reduce nuisance barking. Teaching a "quiet" cue early is worthwhile.

faqs.q: Are Slovensky Cuvacs good apartment dogs?
faqs.a: Slovensky Cuvacs adapt reasonably well to apartment living, particularly if they receive consistent daily walks and indoor enrichment. Their calm nature makes them less disruptive in confined spaces than high-energy large breeds.

faqs.q: How much exercise does a Slovensky Cuvac need per day?
faqs.a: Slovensky Cuvacs need approximately 30–45 minutes of exercise daily. A structured morning walk and an evening sniff walk usually cover their needs. Mental exercise (training sessions, puzzle feeders) counts toward overall stimulation needs and can reduce restless behaviour.

faqs.q: Are Slovensky Cuvacs good running partners?
faqs.a: Slovensky Cuvacs are lower-energy dogs and are better suited to brisk walks or short jogs than distance running. Long runs can cause joint strain in lower-activity breeds — stick to 20–30 minute jogs rather than endurance runs.

faqs.q: What happens if a Slovensky Cuvac doesn't get enough exercise?
faqs.a: Slovensky Cuvacs are less demanding than high-energy breeds, but chronic under-exercise still leads to weight gain and low-level restlessness. Even lower-energy breeds benefit from a consistent daily walk for both physical health and mental stimulation.

faqs.q: Can a Slovensky Cuvac be off-lead?
faqs.a: Off-lead freedom for a Slovensky Cuvac depends on recall reliability, not breed alone. Train recall from puppyhood using long-line sessions before progressing to full off-lead. A standard 20-foot long-line gives freedom while maintaining safety during the training phase.

faqs.q: How much should I feed my Slovensky Cuvac?
faqs.a: A Slovensky Cuvac needs approximately 3–5 cups of dry food per day for an adult, split across two meals. Always follow the feeding guide on your specific formula — calorie density varies significantly between brands. Adjust portions based on body condition: you should be able to feel (but not easily see) the ribs.

faqs.q: How many times a day should I feed a Slovensky Cuvac?
faqs.a: Adult Slovensky Cuvacs should eat twice daily. Puppies (under 6 months) need 3–4 smaller meals per day to support growth and prevent hypoglycaemia, particularly in small breeds. For large and giant breeds, twice daily feeding also reduces the risk of bloat (GDV) compared to one large daily meal.

faqs.q: What is the best food for a Slovensky Cuvac?
faqs.a: Look for a formula carrying an AAFCO adequacy statement for the correct life stage. A named protein source (chicken, turkey, beef, salmon) should appear first in the ingredient list. Lower-energy Slovensky Cuvacs are prone to weight gain — choose a formula with controlled fat content and avoid calorie-dense performance formulas.

faqs.q: When should I switch my Slovensky Cuvac from puppy to adult food?
faqs.a: Large breeds should stay on a large-breed puppy formula until 18–24 months, then transition to an adult formula. Switching too early can disrupt joint development during the growth phase.

faqs.q: Is a Slovensky Cuvac a good dog for first-time owners?
faqs.a: Slovensky Cuvacs are manageable for motivated first-time owners who research the breed, commit to early training, and have realistic expectations about time and cost.

faqs.q: Are Slovensky Cuvacs good family dogs?
faqs.a: Slovensky Cuvacs can be good family dogs when properly socialised. Their suitability depends more on individual temperament and upbringing than breed alone.

faqs.q: Do Slovensky Cuvacs do well when left alone?
faqs.a: Slovensky Cuvacs form strong bonds with their owners and do not do well with extended isolation. Aim for no more than 4–6 hours alone at a time. If your schedule requires longer absences, consider a dog walker, doggy daycare, or a companion dog.

faqs.q: How much time do you need for a Slovensky Cuvac?
faqs.a: Plan for 1–1.5 hours per day dedicated to your Slovensky Cuvac — covering exercise, training, feeding and general interaction. Add 15–30 minutes for grooming 3–4 times weekly. The commitment is consistent year-round, not just when convenient.
